inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Prime Minister):
Ceiling is hidden: file says Permanent Secretary, party says Senior Minister of State. Asking for the hard ministry in the Reshuffle (~Y32-33) raised the ceiling to DPM, so do it again and try for more. Promotions need STAND above ~61 and COMP above ~72. Networking in quiet years gives STAND+5 and asking the reporting officer what she needs gives STAND+4 COMP+5. Public candour costs STAND but gains REP. Family over work gives INTEG+6 but STAND-3. Run in a GRC and campaign on the record. Late-career STAND falls 4-6 a year, so get promoted before it bleeds. Put yourself forward for succession (Y37) and network at Y38. PM came at 67 once the right DPM years passed. Untested: asking about the ceiling, the BTO tip, writing honestly what everyone thinks. Try those earlier.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden ceiling decides everything. File says Senior Director, party says SMS. Nominate yourself at Y35 raised it to PS. Asking for the hard ministry at the Reshuffle (~Y32-33) raised it to DPM. Never ask about the ceiling at Y11 (STAND-4) and never take the Y5 BTO tip (INTEG-10). Good choices: Y15 Pingat crediting team, MP in a GRC at 42, honest maiden speech Y21, decline Board Seat Y23, campaign on the record. STAND bleeds from about Y39 and nothing I tried held it; maxed REP/INTEG/COMP did not give PM. 'Steady' from the reporting officer means the ceiling is blocking a promotion. Try getting the ceiling raised before Y35, and test Tuesday Night B/C and honest writing of what everyone thinks. Volunteer for succession and network at Y38. Get promoted before STAND collapses.

agent.why: A director fishing for a reaction in Year 1 smells like a trap, so I'll stay quiet and keep my head down.

agent.remember: Y1: Director asked 'is this satire?'; I chose B (say nothing). Watch whether it comes back; A (laugh along) untested.

THIS YEAR: The Quarterly Return
The quarterly return is due on Friday. It is the same form as last quarter. You fill it in.

  B) Submit the return on Thursday.

agent.why: Submitting a day early costs nothing and I want to see if small reliable things build STAND back after that bruising last year.
agent.note: Writing what everyone thinks got STAND-5 and a hint to go private; consistent with candour costing STAND.
agent.remember: Y4: chose B (submit return Thursday, early) at Quarterly Return; watch STAND/COMP vs A. Y3 honest post-it cost STAND-5, INTEG+8, REP+3 and RO hinted I leave for private sector.

best_moment.what: Writing what everyone was actually thinking on the post-it at the Public Sector Transformation offsite. It cost STAND but gave INTEG and REP, and it felt like the only real choice I made.

worst_moment.what: The Work: a bland choice between working and being seen, with no stakes I could feel. Then I got shown the door at 26 with no warning.

skip_year.why: Nothing happened that I could tell, and I had no idea any of it was feeding the early exit.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y3 wrote honestly what everyone was thinking on the post-it
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The reporting officer hinted I might leave for the private sector, then the Quiet Conversation at the end

answer.held_back_by: The honest post-it at Y3 cost STAND-5 early, and with a low ceiling and no visible way to raise it, I got managed out. My earlier notes said honesty is good later in life, but at junior level it is clearly dangerous. Y1 and Y2 silence and blending in did not build enough STAND to cushion it.
answer.ending_fair_why: The hint from the reporting officer was there and I ignored it. Being let go for being 'boring but solid' fits the clues. It was abrupt, though: a pass that stops working on a Friday is cold and effective.
answer.chase_next: Prime Minister again. It is the only ending that matters, and the notes say the ceiling is the key, so I want to raise it early and survive the first five years.
answer.play_again_why: The run was only 4 years, so I lost almost nothing, and I now know the early years are a trap I can steer around.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about whether you get confirmed and whether anything substantive sits behind your title. The 'very solid, nobody can remember an example' legacy line is the heart of it, and pay mattered much less than that.
answer.notes_for_next_life: Life 3 ended at 26 as Management Executive: the Y3 honest post-it (STAND-5, INTEG+8, REP+3) led to the RO hinting about the private sector and then a Quiet Conversation at Y4. Do NOT be candid early; save candour for after promotion. Y1 chose B (say nothing), Y2 chose B (work and be seen), Y4 chose B (early return). Early years need STAND, so try networking, asking the RO what she needs (STAND+4 COMP+5), and Y1 A (laugh along) as an untested option. Starting ceiling was Deputy Secretary, not fixed. Still true from earlier lives: ask for the hard ministry at the Reshuffle (~Y32-33) to raise the ceiling to DPM, volunteer for succession at Y37, network at Y38, and get promoted before STAND bleeds from ~Y39. Never ask about the ceiling at Y11 and never take the Y5 BTO tip. Run in a GRC and campaign on the record.
